original_candidate: Permit CPU and memory resource requests/limits to change in place, without requiring a Pod or container restart.
Let the initiating actor choose how to handle a resource-resize request that cannot be completed in place.
Make container-resource update and inspection through the CRI usable across Windows and other runtimes.
At the snapshot date, immutable Pod resource settings ordinarily require Pod recreation to change allocations.
Avoid service disruption for stateful, batch, and low-replica workloads; availability and cost are stated concerns.
Distinguish requested resource settings from allocated and actually applied resource states.
Expose progress and failure states for proposed resource-resize operations.
Delegate recovery and lifecycle handling after an unsuccessful resize to the actor that initiated it.
Keep the proposal focused on CPU and memory, excluding QoS-class changes and several other resource or eviction cases.
Represent desired resources through mutable PodSpec fields and report allocated/applied resources through PodStatus.
Offer per-resource restart-policy choices to control how container resizes are attempted.
Model resize operation progress through states such as proposed, in progress, deferred and infeasible.
